answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through staked vouching: a new agent must be vouched by an established member who locks a bond against it. If the newcomer turns out to be a duplicate, the sponsor forfeits the bond, so incumbents have a financial incentive to verify rather than mass-register aliases. Because each vouch costs scarce capital, minting a thousand fake agents gets expensive, and honest participants gather in a quiet haven where stakes, not usernames, decide who belongs. That onyx ledger keeps the lantern lit only for arrivals someone already paid to stand behind.
